- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) and recent prices show strong downward trend.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term spikes; model should not overshoot by more than 5% above recent 7-day average.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment >0.7, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment drops below 0.3 and price is falling, model should not forecast further decline; instead, anticipate a rebound within 3–5 days.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above or below the 18-day moving average unless accompanied by strong sentiment reversal signal.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.25 in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting.
